svg.text: Turning Data into Systems That Run
This report documents twenty-five independent systems built between 2024 and 2026: retrieval-augmented interfaces, full-stack AI products, learning
experiments, and Linux desktop tooling. Each entry states the problem, the method, and the stack on which it runs. The through-line is practical —
models are treated as components of working software rather than as ends in themselves. All systems are open source, and live demonstrations are
retrieval-augmented generation · computer vision · language models · QML · reproducible software
Applied machine learning rarely fails at the model. It fails at the seams: a retrieval step that returns the right passage but the wrong version of it, an interface that
cannot express uncertainty, a build that nobody else can reproduce. This report is organised around that observation. Section 2 catalogues twenty-five systems
grouped by the problem they address rather than by the technique they use; Section 3 describes how the work is distributed and rebuilt. The selection is deliberately
broad — from a small GNOME extension to a transformer language model written from scratch — because the same engineering discipline applies at every scale.
Table 1 lists each system with its contribution and implementation stack; the index in Section 3 links to source and demonstrations. A filled circle marks a system

Every system is public at github.com/paudelsamir. The index below links to the sources; live demos are hosted on Vercel, Streamlit, or GitHub Pages. This page is
compiled daily from repository metadata by a small build script, so counts and status stay current without manual edits.
